record.paper_title: Tree Spanners on Chordal Graphs: Complexity, Algorithms, Open Problems
record.original_question: A path graph is an intersection graph of paths in a tree. For fixed t >= 3, what is the complexity of deciding whether a path graph admits a tree t-spanner? In particular, what is the status for t = 3 on path graphs that are also strongly chordal?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple connected graph. For an integer t ≥ 1, a spanning subgraph H of G is called a t-spanner of G if for every pair of vertices u, v ∈ V the distance d_H(u, v) in H is at most t · d_G(u, v), where d_G denotes the usual shortest-path distance. A tree t-spanner of G is a t-spanner of G that is a tree (necessarily a spanning tree). The TREE t-SPANNER problem asks, given a graph G, to decide whether G admits a tree t-spanner.

A graph is called a path graph if it is the intersection graph of a family of paths in some host tree (equivalently, the vertices can be put in bijection with paths in a tree so that two vertices are adjacent iff the corresponding paths share at least one vertex). A graph is chordal if every cycle of length at least 4 has a chord. A chordal graph is strongly chordal if every cycle of even length at least 6 has an odd chord (a chord joining two vertices whose distance along the cycle is odd).

Questions:
(a) For each fixed integer t ≥ 3, determine the computational complexity of TREE t-SPANNER when the input graph is restricted to be a path graph.
(b) In particular, determine the computational complexity of TREE 3-SPANNER when the input graph is restricted to be a path graph that is also strongly chordal.
artifact.status_search_result: Multiple references indicate that the complexity status of TREE 3-SPANNER remains a long-standing open problem on chordal graphs, including on the subclass of undirected path graphs that are also strongly chordal. Positive polynomial-time results are known for related but distinct classes (directed path graphs, very strongly chordal graphs, 1-split graphs, chordal graphs of diameter at most 2), but the path-graph and strongly-chordal-path-graph cases for t = 3 (and general fixed t ≥ 3 on path graphs) appear to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Tree spanners on chordal graphs: Complexity and algorithms
status_evidence.snippet: The complexity status of TREE 3-SPANNER still remains open for chordal graphs, even on the subclass of undirected path graphs that are strongly chordal as well.
status_evidence.claim: TREE 3-SPANNER is open on strongly chordal path graphs.

status_evidence.title: An Approximation Algorithm for the Tree t-Spanner Problem on Unweighted Graphs via Generalized Chordal Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: The complexity status of TREE 3-SPANNER remains a long standing open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Complexity of TREE 3-SPANNER remains open in general/relevant chordal subclasses.

status_evidence.title: Characterization and Recognition of Tree 3-Spanner Admissible Directed Path Graphs of Diameter Three
status_evidence.snippet: Work focuses on directed path graphs of diameter three; the broader path-graph case remains unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses only restricted subcases, leaving the path-graph problem open.
